== EXTRACTION RULES (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task C & §5.2; CODEBOOK.md §§1-9; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:
   - If `Retrieval status` is `not_accessible` (or the paper text below says `[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE]`), you MUST set `paper_read = "not accessible"`, set `value = "cannot_tell"`, `where_found = "not accessible"`, and `comment = "full text not accessible"` for ALL 9 fields, and `evidence_quotes = []`. NEVER copy publication year or country from the citation header when the full paper was not read!
2. IF FULL TEXT IS READABLE:
   - Extract each of the 9 fields strictly from the paper text. Write a field value ONLY if the paper explicitly states it; if not stated in the paper, write `"not reported"` in `value` and explain in `comment`. Never guess or infer from context.
   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).
   - `outcome_flags`: Comma-separated list using ONLY exact `CODEBOOK.md` §5 codes actually studied in the paper (`formal_connection`, `water_access`, `sanitation_access`, `service_coverage`, `service_reliability`, `service_quantity`, `service_quality`, `affordability`, `service_continuity`, `application_success`, `refusal`, `delay`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.
3. `where_found` AND `evidence_quotes`:
   - Every field's `where_found` must give exact PDF page(s), section, and/or table/figure number (e.g. `"PDF p. 4, Section 2.2; Table 1, PDF p. 7"`).

evidence_quotes.quote: Agua y Territorio, 24 · pp. 169-189 · Julio - Diciembre 2024 · Universidad de Jaén (España)

El objetivo de este trabajo fue cuantificar los niveles de asequibilidad que garantizan el Derecho Humano al Agua (DHA) en los hogares del Estado, para lo cual se estimaron proporciones de dotación de agua que arriba a los hogares, la calidad y el gasto, utilizando datos institucionales —nacionales, estatales y municipales—, incluidos los emitidos por organismos operadores de agua. Se encontró que existe vulnerabilidad del DHA en los hogares al destinar más del 3 % de sus ingresos a su adquisición.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 8, El agua y sus características principales en Hidalgo
evidence_quotes.quote: El Estado de Hidalgo tiene una población de 3.083.841 habitantes, distribuidos en 84 municipios

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 14, Análisis desde los criterios del DHA en los hogares del Estado de Hidalgo
evidence_quotes.quote: 60 municipios están por encima de los 100 litros de agua por habitante al día, superando las recomendaciones de la OMS, 14 están entre los 50 a 100 litros de agua por habitante al día y 10 en menos de 50 litros de agua por habitante al día.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 16, Análisis desde los criterios del DHA en los hogares del Estado de Hidalgo
evidence_quotes.quote: cabe destacar que cada municipio tiene tarifas de agua diferentes, superando el 3 % del ingreso familiar, lo que hace evidente que desde esta perspectiva el DHA se está vulnerando y en gran medida deriva del gasto que se realiza por la compra de agua embotellada (Mapa 4).

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 16, Análisis desde los criterios del DHA en los hogares del Estado de Hidalgo
evidence_quotes.quote: Sin embargo, aun cuando se consideren dos ingresos en los hogares del Estado de Hidalgo, el gasto en agua para consumo es mayor del 3 %, lo que reafirma que el gasto en agua embotellada es un factor importante

country.comment: Subnational study of the State of Hidalgo, Mexico (all 84 municipalities), using national minimum-wage and bottled-water expenditure benchmarks.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Resumen/Abstract; PDF p. 8, 'El agua y sus características principales en Hidalgo'

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative descriptive estimates (proportions, L/inhabitant/day, MXN/month, and % of 1 and 2 minimum wages); no statistical confidence intervals or p-values are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Although official piped water coverage in Hidalgo is 96% (66.9% inside dwellings, 29.1% on plot) and sewerage coverage is 94% (2020 Census), Human Right to Water criteria are not fulfilled in quantity, quality, or affordability: based on 2022 REPDA concessions across 84 municipalities, 60 municipalities exceed 100 L/inhabitant/day, 14 have 50-100 L/inhabitant/day, and 10 fall below the 50 L/inhabitant/day minimum (lowest in Metepec at 8 L/inhabitant/day, Tlahuiltepa at 13, and Tizayuca at 14), with intermittent delivery every third day ('tandeo'). Combining statutory water/sewerage tariffs and bottled-water spending, monthly household water expenditure under CAASIM rose from 227.23 MXN in 2013 (5.04% of 1 minimum wage; 2.52% of 2 minimum wages) to 403.65 MXN in 2022 (134.44 MXN tariff + 269.21 MXN bottled water), reaching 8.95% of 1 minimum wage and 4.48% of 2 minimum wages, and exceeding the 3% HRW affordability threshold across all 84 municipalities in 2022 (ranging from 6% in Chilcuautla to 12.5% in Tianguistengo under 1 minimum wage).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 11, 'El agua y sus características principales en Hidalgo'; PDF pp. 14-17, 'Análisis desde los criterios del DHA en los hogares del Estado de Hidalgo', Tables 1-2, Table 4, and Mapa 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling for a non-experimental legal-empirical / descriptive municipal study is at most 2. Assigned 1 because the study documents descriptive accounting relationships between statutory municipal tariffs, aggregate REPDA water-concession volumes, and municipal water sufficiency/affordability indicators (using imputed national average bottled-water expenditure and statutory minimum wages) rather than directly observing household-level billing, tariff enforcement, or administrative permitting processes.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 7-8, 'Materiales y métodos'; PDF pp. 14-18, 'Análisis desde los criterios del DHA' and 'Conclusiones'

mechanism_flags.comment: Directly compiles and analyzes statutory municipal and intermunicipal (CAASIM) water, sewerage, and sanitation tariffs (Ley de ingresos, cuotas y tarifas municipales 2022, decrees 55-170) and critiques tariff designs that fail to account for household size/composition or low-income basic consumption.
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 7-8, 'Materiales y métodos'; PDF pp. 15-18, Table 4, Mapa 4, and 'Conclusiones'

outcome_flags.comment: Evaluates household water affordability (% of 1 and 2 minimum wages vs. 3% threshold), per-capita water supply quantity (L/inhabitant/day vs. 50 and 100 L thresholds), surface/groundwater quality (DBO, DQO, SST, fecal coliforms, heavy metals/arsenic/fluorides), municipal water/sewerage coverage, piped/hauled household water access, and intermittent 'tandeo' service continuity.
outcome_flags.value: affordability, service_quantity, service_quality, service_coverage, water_access, service_continuity
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 7-8, 'Materiales y métodos'; PDF pp. 11-17, Gráficas 2 & 4, Mapas 3 & 4, Tablas 1, 2 & 4

publication_year.comment: Published in Agua y Territorio, Issue 24, pp. 169-189, Julio - Diciembre 2024 (received 02/01/2023, accepted 23/10/2023).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: The study is a legal-empirical / doctrinal-empirical compliance assessment evaluating Mexican constitutional Human Right to Water guarantees (Arts. 4 and 115), the Ley de Aguas Nacionales (REPDA water concessions), and 2022 statutory municipal tariff decrees (decrees 55-170) using aggregate descriptive municipal indicators rather than an analytical exposure-outcome cross-sectional survey/regression or quasi-experimental design.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF pp. 4-8, 'Introducción', 'DHA en México y su medición', and 'Materiales y métodos'

sample_size.comment: Covers all 84 municipalities of Hidalgo State (total population 3,083,841 per 2020 Census; 15 municipalities served by CAASIM), alongside a 10-year annual series (2013-2022) of minimum wages, CAASIM tariffs, and estimated household water expenditures.
sample_size.value: 84 municipalities of Hidalgo State (3,083,841 inhabitants); 10-year tariff and household expenditure series (2013-2022)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 7, 'Materiales y métodos'; PDF p. 8, 'El agua y sus características principales en Hidalgo'; Tablas 1-4, PDF pp. 15-16

study_design.comment: Described by the authors as a descriptive investigation ('investigación de carácter descriptivo') framed under the Human Right to Water (DHA). Combines statutory municipal water/sewerage tariff schedules (2022 municipal revenue laws, decrees 55-170, and CAASIM tariffs) and federal water-rights concession records (REPDA) with census (INEGI 2020), bottled-water expenditure (MOHOMA 2017), minimum-wage (CONASAMI 2013-2022), and water-quality (SINA/CONAGUA) databases across Hidalgo's 84 municipalities without inferential regression or causal comparator.
study_design.value: Descriptive legal-empirical compliance study using municipal administrative, statutory tariff, and census databases
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 4, 'Introducción'; PDF pp. 7-8, 'Materiales y métodos'
